text:
nora: Quick report from user calls: auth behavior across our SDKs/CLI is confusing when people use org vs project keys + ephemeral rotation.

joel: TL;DR?

nora: Repro in 3 lines: 1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_xxx and REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-blue; 2) create project-scoped key and rotate; 3) long-running dev shell still sends org_xxx, but ephemeral CI runners pick up new key.

tara: I saw this with local sample-apps too. Our JS SDK prefers env, but the Go CLI persisted a "last-active" entry that overrides env for the running process.

joel: That was a ux decision to reduce friction, but it's causing silent auth drift. Users rotate keys expecting immediate effect.

nora: Two small fixes I want: (A) make `rw auth rotate` update the in-process resolution when executed from an interactive shell (unless `--no-shell`), and (B) add `REDWOOD_DEBUG_AUTH=1` output like: `lookup_order=env,file,metadata resolved_key_id=proj_****` (masking full key).

tara: Also add a short troubleshooting blurb to sample-app README explaining scoping and how to check what was used with the debug env.

joel: Agree. We should also add an integration test matrix that runs a tiny container with combinations: env set/unset, creds-file present/absent, last-active present/absent — assert resolved key id and precedence.

devex-bot: Reminder: changes to credential resolution must include a migration note and changelog entry.

nora: I'll file two PRs: CLI change + debug flag; docs + test matrix. Joel/Tara can review. Thanks! :thumbsup:
